question_text: Which budget functions show the largest year-over-year increases?
reference_sql:

    b1.function_name, 
    b1.fiscal_year, 
    b1.outlay_amount AS current_year_outlay, 
    b2.outlay_amount AS previous_year_outlay, 
    (b1.outlay_amount - b2.outlay_amount) AS year_over_year_increase
FROM 
    budget_outlays b1
JOIN 
    budget_outlays b2 
ON 
    b1.function_name = b2.function_name 
    AND b1.fiscal_year = b2.fiscal_year + 1
WHERE 
    b1.outlay_amount IS NOT NULL 
    AND b2.outlay_amount IS NOT NULL

question_text: Which economic indicators move in opposite directions?
reference_sql:
SELECT a.industry_name AS industry_name_a, b.industry_name AS industry_name_b
FROM industry_gdp a
JOIN industry_gdp b ON a.year = b.year AND a.industry_code < b.industry_code
WHERE a.gdp_value IS NOT NULL AND b.gdp_value IS NOT NULL

question_text: Which industries show higher GDP growth rates than the national average?
reference_sql:
WITH national_gdp_growth AS (
    SELECT 
        (MAX(numeric_value) - MIN(numeric_value)) / MIN(numeric_value) * 100 AS national_growth_rate
    FROM 
        time_series_data
    WHERE 
        category = 'GDP' AND 
        numeric_value IS NOT NULL
),
industry_growth AS (
    SELECT 
        category AS industry,
        (MAX(numeric_value) - MIN(numeric_value)) / MIN(numeric_value) * 100 AS industry_growth_rate
    FROM 
        time_series_data
    WHERE 
        category != 'GDP' AND 
        numeric_value IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY 
        category
)
SELECT 
    industry, 
    industry_growth_rate
FROM 
    industry_growth, national_gdp_growth
WHERE 
    industry_growth_rate > national_growth_rate
ORDER BY 
    industry_growth_rate DESC
LIMIT 20;

question_text: Which industries contribute disproportionately to economic growth vs. their size?
reference_sql:
SELECT 
    tsd.category AS industry,
    SUM(tsd.numeric_value) AS total_gdp_contribution,
    bo.total_outlays,
    (SUM(tsd.numeric_value) / bo.total_outlays) AS contribution_ratio
FROM 
    time_series_data tsd
JOIN 
    (SELECT 
        function_name, 
        SUM(outlay_amount) AS total_outlays
     FROM 
        budget_outlays
     WHERE 
        function_name IS NOT NULL
     GROUP BY 
        function_name) bo
ON 
    tsd.category = bo.function_name
WHERE 
    tsd.category IS NOT NULL
    AND tsd.source = 'BEA'
GROUP BY 
    tsd.category, bo.total_outlays
HAVING 
    contribution_ratio > 1.0
ORDER BY 
    contribution_ratio DESC
LIMIT 20;

question_text: How do projected vs. actual spending figures compare across categories?
reference_sql:
SELECT 
    b.function_name AS category,
    SUM(b.outlay_amount) AS total_outlays,
    t.numeric_value AS projected_spending,
    SUM(b.outlay_amount) - t.numeric_value AS difference
FROM 
    budget_outlays b
JOIN 
    time_series_data t ON b.function_name = t.category
WHERE 
    b.fiscal_year IS NOT NULL
    AND b.outlay_amount IS NOT NULL
    AND t.numeric_value IS NOT NULL
    AND t.source = 'Projected'
GROUP BY 
    b.function_name, t.numeric_value
HAVING 
    ABS(SUM(b.outlay_amount) - t.numeric_value) > 0
ORDER BY 
    ABS(SUM(b.outlay_amount) - t.numeric_value) DESC
LIMIT 20;

question_text: What patterns emerge in budget allocations during election years?
reference_sql:
SELECT 
    fiscal_year,
    CASE WHEN fiscal_year % 4 = 0 THEN 'Election Year' ELSE 'Non-Election Year' END AS year_type,
    SUM(outlay_amount) AS total_budget_outlays,
    COUNT(DISTINCT function_name) AS number_of_functions,
    AVG(outlay_amount) AS avg_outlay_per_function,
    MAX(outlay_amount) AS largest_single_outlay,
    function_name AS largest_outlay_function
FROM budget_outlays b1
WHERE outlay_amount IS NOT NULL
    AND fiscal_year >= 2000
    AND outlay_amount = (
        SELECT MAX(b2.outlay_amount) 
        FROM budget_outlays b2 
        WHERE b2.fiscal_year = b1.fiscal_year
    )
GROUP BY fiscal_year, year_type, function_name
ORDER BY fiscal_year DESC;

question_text: When do wage growth and productivity growth move in opposite directions?

    SUM(CASE WHEN tsd.indicator_id = 'productivity_growth' THEN tsd.numeric_value ELSE 0 END) AS total_productivity_growth

question_text: Which industries show correlated growth patterns?

WITH IndustryGrowth AS (

        year, 
        SUM(gdp_value) AS total_gdp
    FROM

    WHERE 
        gdp_value IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY

),
IndustryGrowthRate AS (
    SELECT 
        ig1.industry_name,
        ig1.year,
        (ig1.total_gdp - COALESCE(ig2.total_gdp, 0)) / COALESCE(ig2.total_gdp, 1) AS growth_rate
    FROM 
        IndustryGrowth ig1
    LEFT JOIN 
        IndustryGrowth ig2 ON ig1.industry_name = ig2.industry_name AND ig1.year = ig2.year + 1
)
SELECT 
    ig1.industry_name AS industry1,
    ig2.industry_name AS industry2,
    COUNT(*) AS correlated_years
FROM 
    IndustryGrowthRate ig1
JOIN 
    IndustryGrowthRate ig2 ON ig1.year = ig2.year AND ig1.industry_name < ig2.industry_name
WHERE 
    ABS(ig1.growth_rate - ig2.growth_rate) < 0.05
GROUP BY 
    ig1.industry_name, ig2.industry_name
HAVING 
    COUNT(*) > 1
ORDER BY 
    correlated_years DESC
LIMIT 10;

question_text: How do spending patterns during economic expansions compare to those during contractions?
reference_sql:
WITH gdp_growth AS (
    SELECT 
        year,
        SUM(gdp_value * unit_multiplier) AS total_gdp
    FROM 
        industry_gdp
    WHERE 
        gdp_value IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY 
        year
),
gdp_change AS (
    SELECT 
        year,
        total_gdp,
        LAG(total_gdp) OVER (ORDER BY year) AS previous_gdp,
        (total_gdp - LAG(total_gdp) OVER (ORDER BY year)) / LAG(total_gdp) OVER (ORDER BY year) AS gdp_growth_rate
    FROM 
        gdp_growth
),
economic_periods AS (
    SELECT 
        year,
        CASE 
            WHEN gdp_growth_rate > 0 THEN 'expansion'
            ELSE 'contraction'
        END AS economic_period
    FROM 
        gdp_change
    WHERE 
        gdp_growth_rate IS NOT NULL
),
spending_patterns AS (
    SELECT 
        b.fiscal_year,
        e.economic_period,
        SUM(b.outlay_amount) AS total_outlay
    FROM 
        budget_outlays b
    JOIN 
        economic_periods e ON b.fiscal_year = e.year
    WHERE 
        b.outlay_amount IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY 
        b.fiscal_year, e.economic_period
)
SELECT 
    economic_period,
    AVG(total_outlay) AS avg_outlay
FROM 
    spending_patterns
GROUP BY 
    economic_period
ORDER BY 
    economic_period;

question_text: Which sectors show the strongest vs. weakest links to government spending?

WITH sector_spending AS (
    SELECT

        COUNT(*) as years_of_data
    FROM budget_outlays

    HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3
),
gdp_data AS (

        AVG(numeric_value) as avg_gdp
    FROM time_series_data 
    WHERE category = 'GDP' 
    AND numeric_value IS NOT NULL
),
sector_correlation AS (
    SELECT 
        s.sector,
        s.total_outlays,
        s.avg_annual_outlays,
        (s.total_outlays / g.avg_gdp) * 100 as spending_to_gdp_ratio,
        CASE 
            WHEN s.total_outlays > (SELECT AVG(total_outlays) * 1.5 FROM sector_spending) THEN 'Strongest Link'
            WHEN s.total_outlays < (SELECT AVG(total_outlays) * 0.5 FROM sector_spending) THEN 'Weakest Link'
            ELSE 'Moderate Link'
        END as spending_strength
    FROM sector_spending s
    CROSS JOIN gdp_data g
)
SELECT 
    sector,
    total_outlays,
    spending_to_gdp_ratio,
    spending_strength
FROM sector_correlation
WHERE spending_strength IN ('Strongest Link', 'Weakest Link');

question_text: Which budget categories show immediate vs. delayed policy effects?
reference_sql:
WITH recent_outlays AS (
    SELECT 
        function_name, 
        fiscal_year,

    FROM 
        budget_outlays
    WHERE 
        fiscal_year >= (SELECT MAX(fiscal_year) FROM budget_outlays) - 1
    GROUP BY 
        function_name, fiscal_year
),
previous_outlays AS (
    SELECT 
        function_name, 
        fiscal_year, 
        SUM(outlay_amount) AS total_outlays
    FROM 
        budget_outlays
    WHERE 
        fiscal_year < (SELECT MAX(fiscal_year) FROM budget_outlays) - 1
    GROUP BY 
        function_name, fiscal_year
),
outlay_changes AS (
    SELECT 
        r.function_name,
        r.total_outlays AS recent_outlays,
        COALESCE(p.total_outlays, 0) AS previous_outlays,
        r.total_outlays - COALESCE(p.total_outlays, 0) AS outlay_change
    FROM 
        recent_outlays r
    LEFT JOIN 
        previous_outlays p ON r.function_name = p.function_name
)
SELECT 
    function_name,
    recent_outlays,
    previous_outlays,
    outlay_change,
    CASE 
        WHEN outlay_change > 0 THEN 'Immediate Effect'
        ELSE 'Delayed Effect'
    END AS policy_effect
FROM

LIMIT 20;

question_text: How do the largest spending categories compare in growth rates vs. absolute changes?

  FROM budget_outlays

  GROUP BY function_name
  HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT fiscal_year) >= 2
),
largest_categories AS (
  SELECT 
    function_name,
    first_year,
    last_year,
    first_year_outlays,
    last_year_outlays,
    total_outlays,
    (last_year_outlays - first_year_outlays) as absolute_change,

      WHEN first_year_outlays > 0

  FROM spending_by_category
  ORDER BY total_outlays DESC
  LIMIT 10
)

  growth_rate_percent,

question_text: How do acceleration vs. deceleration patterns compare across indicators?
reference_sql:

  SELECT 
    indicator_id,
    year,
    numeric_value,
    LAG(numeric_value) OVER (PARTITION BY indicator_id ORDER BY year) as prev_value,
    numeric_value - LAG(numeric_value) OVER (PARTITION BY indicator_id ORDER BY year) as change_value
  FROM time_series_data 
  WHERE numeric_value IS NOT NULL 
    AND period_type = 'annual'
),
acceleration_patterns AS (
  SELECT 
    indicator_id,
    year,
    change_value,
    LAG(change_value) OVER (PARTITION BY indicator_id ORDER BY year) as prev_change,
    CASE 
      WHEN change_value > LAG(change_value) OVER (PARTITION BY indicator_id ORDER BY year) THEN 'acceleration'
      WHEN change_value < LAG(change_value) OVER (PARTITION BY indicator_id ORDER BY year) THEN 'deceleration'
      ELSE 'stable'
    END as pattern_type
  FROM yearly_changes
  WHERE change_value IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
  indicator_id,
  pattern_type,

WITH normal_periods AS (
    SELECT 
        series_id, 
        year, 
        AVG(numeric_value) AS avg_value
    FROM

    SELECT 
        series_id,

        AVG(numeric_value) AS avg_value
    FROM 
        time_series_data

        n.series_id AS normal_series_id,
        c.series_id AS crisis_series_id,
        n.year AS normal_year,
        c.year AS crisis_year,
        n.avg_value AS normal_avg_value,
        c.avg_value AS crisis_avg_value

        normal_periods n

        crisis_periods c ON n.series_id = c.series_id AND n.year = c.year
)
SELECT 
    normal_series_id,
    crisis_series_id,
    normal_year,
    crisis_year,
    normal_avg_value,
    crisis_avg_value,
    (normal_avg_value - crisis_avg_value) AS value_difference

question_text: Which transition patterns are reversible vs. irreversible?
reference_sql:
SELECT 
    t1.function_name,
    t1.fiscal_year as start_year,
    t2.fiscal_year as end_year,
    t1.outlay_amount as start_amount,

    CASE 
        WHEN ABS((t2.outlay_amount - t1.outlay_amount) / t1.outlay_amount * 100) < 10 THEN 'Reversible'

        ELSE 'Potentially Reversible'
    END as transition_pattern
FROM budget_outlays t1
JOIN budget_outlays t2 ON t1.function_name = t2.function_name 
    AND t2.fiscal_year = t1.fiscal_year + 5
WHERE t1.outlay_amount IS NOT NULL 
    AND t2.outlay_amount IS NOT NULL
    AND t1.outlay_amount > 0
ORDER BY ABS(change_percent) DESC
LIMIT 20;

question_text: Which indicators show pro-cyclical vs. counter-cyclical patterns?
reference_sql:
WITH gdp_growth AS (
    SELECT 
        year, 
        (gdp_value - LAG(gdp_value) OVER (ORDER BY year)) / LAG(gdp_value) OVER (ORDER BY year) AS gdp_growth_rate
    FROM 
        industry_gdp
    WHERE 
        gdp_value IS NOT NULL
),
indicator_growth AS (
    SELECT 
        indicator_id, 
        year, 
        (numeric_value - LAG(numeric_value) OVER (PARTITION BY indicator_id ORDER BY year)) / LAG(numeric_value) OVER (PARTITION BY indicator_id ORDER BY year) AS indicator_growth_rate
    FROM 
        time_series_data
    WHERE 
        numeric_value IS NOT NULL
),
correlation_analysis AS (
    SELECT 
        i.indicator_id,
        AVG(i.indicator_growth_rate * g.gdp_growth_rate) AS correlation_coefficient
    FROM 
        indicator_growth i
    JOIN 
        gdp_growth g ON i.year = g.year
    GROUP BY 
        i.indicator_id
)
SELECT 
    indicator_id,
    CASE 
        WHEN correlation_coefficient > 0 THEN 'Pro-cyclical'
        WHEN correlation_coefficient < 0 THEN 'Counter-cyclical'
        ELSE 'No clear pattern'
    END AS cycle_pattern
FROM 
    correlation_analysis
ORDER BY 
    correlation_coefficient DESC;

question_text: Which indicators show linear vs. nonlinear response patterns?
reference_sql:
WITH linear_patterns AS (
    SELECT 
        category,
        COUNT(*) AS data_points,
        SUM(numeric_value) AS total_value,
        AVG(numeric_value) AS avg_value,
        MIN(numeric_value) AS min_value,
        MAX(numeric_value) AS max_value
    FROM 
        time_series_data
    WHERE 
        numeric_value IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY 
        category
    HAVING 
        (MAX(numeric_value) - MIN(numeric_value)) / NULLIF(AVG(numeric_value), 0) < 0.1
),
nonlinear_patterns AS (
    SELECT 
        category,
        COUNT(*) AS data_points,
        SUM(numeric_value) AS total_value,
        AVG(numeric_value) AS avg_value,
        MIN(numeric_value) AS min_value,
        MAX(numeric_value) AS max_value
    FROM 
        time_series_data
    WHERE 
        numeric_value IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY 
        category
    HAVING 
        (MAX(numeric_value) - MIN(numeric_value)) / NULLIF(AVG(numeric_value), 0) >= 0.1
)
SELECT 
    'Linear' AS pattern_type,
    category,
    data_points,
    total_value,
    avg_value,
    min_value,
    max_value
FROM 
    linear_patterns
UNION ALL
SELECT 
    'Nonlinear' AS pattern_type,
    category,
    data_points,
    total_value,
    avg_value,
    min_value,
    max_value
FROM 
    nonlinear_patterns
ORDER BY 
    pattern_type ASC, data_points DESC
LIMIT 20;
